question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 16 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: A sudden increase in connection pool exhaustion warnings caused the p95 latency spike.
why_chain: The connection pool exhaustion warnings indicate a failure in the database connection management.
This failure is likely due to the new release or version of the service.
The new release or version of the service is the cause of the p95 latency spike.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in request volume did not cause the p95 latency spike.
why_chain: The request volume for service auth stayed about the same before and after the change.
The error rate for service auth increased, indicating a different issue.
The error rate increase is more likely the cause of the p95 latency spike.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency was due to a configuration change.
ruled_out.reason: The change in p95 latency occurred at the same time as the change point, and the error rate increased, suggesting a configuration change is unlikely.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency was due to a deployment of a new release or version.
ruled_out.reason: The p95 latency spike occurred at the same time as the change point, and the error rate increased, suggesting a deployment is likely the cause.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency was due to a traffic spike.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume for service auth stayed about the same before and after the change, and the error rate increased, suggesting a traffic spike is unlikely.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency was due to an infrastructure issue.
ruled_out.reason: The p95 latency spike occurred at the same time as the change point, and the error rate increased, suggesting an infrastructure issue is unlikely.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for service auth rose from 90 ms to 268 ms (+197%), with a change point at 2026-03-16T14:35:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service auth: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for service auth stayed about the same (1125 per 5 min before, 1299 per 5 min after, +15%).
At the same time, error rate for service auth rose (0.38% before, 0.60% after, +61%).
p95 latency above SLO on auth (auth; 15 min after the change; record R014; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
auth: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (auth, ap-south; 5 min after the change; record R013; fit: describes a symptom, not a change)
auth: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (auth, eu-west; 19 min after the change; record R015; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
auth: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (auth, us-east; 27 min after the change; record R016; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)

reasons: ✗ No deploy, config change, ticket or alert lines up with the change.
✓ 4 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.

Monitor the database connection pool and ensure it is properly configured and monitored.
